Saudi Sick Leave Pay Calculator

Enter your actual wage and the sick days since the first sick leave of your sick-leave year to see your sick pay and the deduction.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Calculate your sick leave pay

Basic salary plus fixed allowances (housing and transport).
All days since your first sick leave, consecutive or separate.
To see when your sick-leave year ends.

Sick leave tiers in Saudi Arabia

Days in the sick-leave yearPay
First 30 daysFull pay
Next 60 daysThree-quarters pay
Following 30 daysUnpaid

Example: actual wage SAR 9,000 and 45 sick days. Daily wage = SAR 300.
30 days on full pay = SAR 9,000; 15 days at three-quarters = 15 × 225 = SAR 3,375.
Sick pay = SAR 12,375 against SAR 13,500 of normal pay, a deduction of SAR 1,125.

Frequently asked questions

When does the sick-leave year start?

From the date of your first sick leave — not from 1 January or your joining date. If your first sick leave was on 10 March 2026, the year ends on 9 March 2027, and the first sick leave after that opens a new year with a full balance.

What wage is sick pay based on in Saudi Arabia?

The actual wage — basic salary plus fixed allowances such as housing and transport — because Article 2 of the Labour Law gives "wage" the meaning of the actual wage wherever it appears.

Do I get paid sick leave during probation?

The text sets no service requirement and does not exclude probation. Sick days are not counted as part of probation, which is extended by the same period within the limits the law allows.

Are separate sick days added together?

Yes. Article 117 counts days whether consecutive or separate within the same sick-leave year.

Did Article 117 change in the 2025 amendments?

No. The Labour Law amendments in force since 19 February 2025 did not touch Article 117, so the tiers are still 30, 60 and 30 days.

What if I work elsewhere while on sick leave?

Article 118 allows the employer to withhold your pay for the leave period or recover what it paid you.

Sources

  • Ministry of Human Resources — conditions of work, text of Articles 117 and 118 (Arabic)
  • HRDF — Saudi Labour Law, Articles 2, 117 and 118 (English)
  • Umm Al-Qura — Labour Law amendments by Royal Decree M/44, which do not include Article 117 (Arabic)
